If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract downward bias.

If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% at the 16–30 day horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon (21–30 days) to capture momentum continuation.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late horizon to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is consistently bullish but price is trending down, reduce forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon to align with sentiment-price divergence.
